objective.text: Distinguish a CSRF failure from an authentication failure on a state-changing route.

difficulty.rationale: Identify a failed request-integrity check independently of whether a user is authenticated.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: In Laravel 13.40, an authenticated browser user sends a protected POST without a CSRF token or Sec-Fetch-Site header. The route is not exempt, testing bypass is off, and normal token fallback is enabled. Under default exception handling, what does a 419 indicate?

options.text: The request-forgery check failed; authentication alone does not satisfy it.
options.rationale: With neither accepted origin metadata nor a matching token, this protected POST fails the token check even if a user is authenticated.
A 419 token-mismatch response does not establish a credential-verification failure.
options.misconception: A 419 token-mismatch response does not establish a credential-verification failure.

options.rationale: A policy denial normally concerns authorization; the stated failure occurs at the request-forgery boundary.
options.misconception: A policy denial normally concerns authorization; the stated failure occurs at the request-forgery boundary.

options.text: The route does not support POST.
options.rationale: Unsupported HTTP methods produce a routing failure such as 405, not the stated token-mismatch status.
options.misconception: Unsupported HTTP methods produce a routing failure such as 405, not the stated token-mismatch status.
